mutants.reason: Inverting the reset test in the RX sequencer makes reset not clear the sequencer. A partly received frame survives reset, and normal operation is held in reset state.
Changing && to || makes o_tx_ready rise at the wrong time. It rises early whenever bit_idx is 9 or cnt is 1, instead of only in the last stop-bit cycle.
While idle, o_txd would be driven low instead of staying high. The idle line and the stop bit at the end of a frame are broken.
The first synchronizer flop would reset to 0. A spurious start bit is detected after reset release, even when the line is idle high.
With != on the counter, o_tx_ready is raised at the wrong cycle of the stop bit (counter not equal to 1). The ready timing E0+10N-1 is wrong.
Inverting the bit-count test moves the data-to-stop transition to the wrong bit. The stop sample M and the delivery time V are wrong and the byte is garbled.
Inverting the counter-nonzero test makes the counter decrement only at zero and load a new bit at nonzero. Bit width and frame length are wrong.
At acceptance o_txd would stay 1 instead of going to the start bit 0. There is no start bit in the cycle after E0.
o_rx_frame_err would reset to 1 instead of 0. The reset output value is wrong.
The synchronizer reset is inverted, so the flops are not reset when i_rst_n=0 and instead load i_rxd. The first-edge start detection and the reset behaviour are wrong.
o_tx_ready would be driven 0 where it should return to 1 in the last stop-bit cycle. The transmitter never becomes ready again.
frame_done is never asserted at M. No byte is ever loaded and delivered.
With the index test inverted, o_tx_ready is raised in the wrong bit (any bit other than the stop bit). The ready timing is wrong.
The whole ready condition is negated, so o_tx_ready is raised at every counter step except the final stop-bit one. It goes high early and the frame is cut short.
o_tx_ready would stay 1 after acceptance instead of dropping to 0. Another byte can be accepted during a frame.
o_rx_valid would reset to 1 instead of 0. A byte appears valid during and after reset.
The start condition is inverted. Starts are detected when there is no falling edge and ignored when there is one.
The shift register would fill with 0 instead of 1. The stop bit (frame bit 9) is sent as 0, so the stop bit is wrong.

r_rxd_prev is reset to 0 instead of 1, but r_rxd_sync is still reset to 1. So w_rx_start_fall = prev & ~sync is 0 while in reset or in the cycle just after release. At the first edge R1 prev reloads from sync (=1) in both versions. The first-edge start detection is therefore identical at the ports.
The idle branch condition is inverted. Idle forces o_txd to 1 only during a frame, and the frame is run when idle. Idle and frame behaviour are both broken.
o_rx_overrun would reset to 1 instead of 0. The output has the wrong value during reset.
The bit-count test is negated, so the receiver goes to the stop state after the first data bit and then keeps counting. Sampling points and delivery are wrong.
o_txd would reset to 0 instead of 1. The line is low during reset and an abandoned frame does not return the line high.
The second synchronizer flop would reset to 0. After reset a start fall (prev=1, sync=0) is detected spuriously.
The accept condition is negated, so a byte is accepted when i_tx_valid=0 or o_tx_ready=0 and not accepted at the handshake. Nothing is transmitted correctly.
The default for w_rx_frame_done would be 1, so frames are signalled complete in every state. This gives spurious loads and overrun pulses.
The nonzero test in the data state is inverted. The counter decrements only at zero and the data bit is sampled at the wrong edges. The byte is wrong.
o_tx_ready would reset to 0 instead of 1. The transmitter is not ready in and after reset.
On load o_rx_valid would be set to 0 rather than 1. A received byte is never presented as valid.
The TX reset test is inverted. Reset does not abandon a frame or set o_txd/o_tx_ready, and the normal logic is held in reset when reset is released.
When the consumer takes the byte, o_rx_valid would stay 1 instead of dropping to 0. A taken byte appears again.
The load condition is inverted. Bytes are loaded when no frame completes and not loaded when one does.
The reset test of the holding-register block is inverted. The outputs are not reset on reset and are cleared during normal run.
The start-bit recheck at T0+H is inverted. Glitches are accepted as starts and valid start bits are rejected.
The nonzero test in the stop state is inverted. The stop sample M and the delivery edge V are at the wrong time.
The nonzero test in the start state is inverted. The start-bit check at T0+H is at the wrong time and so are all later sample edges.
